task.description: Write test/specs/REQ-030.md and test code for REQ-030's implementation (branch feature/WF02-REQ030-20260817). Note: test/letflow/definitions_test.exs already exists (from REQ-041) -- extend it with REQ-030's coverage, don't create a duplicate/conflicting file. This module operates on real Postgres tenant schemas (process_definitions) -- follow this project's established real-Postgres test pattern (e.g. test/letflow/definitions/snapshot_store_test.exs from REQ-033, or test/letflow/event_store_test.exs from REQ-025), no mocking.
acceptance_criteria: create/1 with a graph that fails REQ-028's validateGraph() writes zero rows and returns the collected violations, not a generic error

two concurrent create/1 calls with identical (name, version) result in exactly one success and one duplicate-error, demonstrated with an actual concurrent test or the ON CONFLICT code path cited explicitly if concurrency can't be exercised
activate/1 on a DRAFT definition atomically deprecates any prior ACTIVE version of the same name in the same transaction, verified by reading both rows after the call
activate/1 called twice on the same already-ACTIVE definition returns the no-op/AlreadyActive result both times, never an error

every one of the 9 forbidden-transition cells in definition.md's authoritative state transition table is tested and rejected (not just 4 -- REQ-030's own AC5 text undercounts this, both CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR and SECURITY-REVIEWER independently confirmed the real table has 9 forbidden cells)
activate/1's signature includes a nil-able/optional service-scope-validation hook parameter that REQ-031 wires in, documented explicitly in the moduledoc as the SVC-03 integration point

get_active_by_name/1 against a name with an ACTIVE version returns that definition; against a name with only DRAFT/DEPRECATED/ARCHIVED versions returns a not-found error, not the most recent non-active row
list/1 with a stage filter returns only rows whose stage column exactly matches the filter value, combinable with a simultaneous name and/or status filter in the same call

result.summary: Wrote test/specs/REQ-030.md and test/letflow/definitions/store_test.exs (27 DB-backed tests, real Postgres via Letflow.DataCase + provisioned_tenant/1, mirroring snapshot_store_test.exs's/event_store_test.exs's established pattern), and extended the existing test/letflow/definitions_test.exs (REQ-041's pure file) with 2 doc-content describe blocks (13 pure tests total). Re-verified the requirement has 9 acceptance criteria (not 8 or 4) directly against docs/requirements.yaml lines 1408-1417. Every AC has at least one test that would fail if the behavior broke: AC1 (3 tests, one per validate_graph/1, validate_node_attributes/1, validate_edge_conditions/1 -- closing the REQ-029 two-validator gap the design doc flags), AC2 (genuine Task.async concurrency, not the code-path-citation fallback), AC3 (both rows re-read from Postgres after the call), AC4 (3 sequential calls, all asserted non-error), AC5 (all 9 forbidden-transition cells individually tested, not 4 -- the 3 X->DRAFT cells with no direct function to attempt them are proven via a never-yields-:draft check across all 3 mutating functions), AC6 (4 behavioral tests including hook-not-called-on-wrong-paths, plus 2 pure moduledoc tests), AC7 (3 tests including the deprecated-only not-most-recent-non-active case), AC8 (all 3 filters combined in one call), AC9 (3 behavioral tests plus 1 pure moduledoc test). Also added an optional regression test for SECURITY-REVIEWER's filed activate/2 TOCTOU finding (design doc SS6.2) -- this run's actual mix test execution empirically triggered the real Postgres unique-violation race, not merely a theoretical pass. All 40 tests (13 pure + 27 DB-backed) pass against real Postgres. Full file compiles clean under 'MIX_ENV=test mix do compile --warnings-as-errors + test --warnings-as-errors' (0 warnings after fixing one dead-default-argument warning and shortening several describe/test name combinations that were approaching Erlang's 255-byte atom limit -- one combination originally exceeded it and crashed compilation, since ExUnit derives a function-name atom from "test " <> describe <> " " <> test-name).
